flags.note: The participle שׁוֹתְקִים precedes its subject כּוּלָּם, which follows Greek syntax. Natural Hebrew would place the subject before the participle: כּוּלָּם שׁוֹתְקִים בַּשָּׁמַיִם.
The construct שֶׁל זָהָב instead of the expected construct state מַחְתּוֹת זָהָב shows influence from Greek genitive constructions, though שֶׁל is attested in late Hebrew.
The word order 'wells of-water' is awkward in Hebrew. Natural Hebrew would use construct state בְּאֵרוֹת הַמַּיִם or simply הַבְּאֵרוֹת, as מַיִם is redundant after בְּאֵרוֹת.
The phrase עַל יַד literally 'by the hand of' is a calque from Greek ἐκ/ὑπό + genitive meaning causation. Natural Hebrew would use מִן הַמַּיִם or בַּמַּיִם for death caused by waters.

The relative clause שֶׁצְּרִיכִים modifying הַשּׁוֹפָרֹת creates ambiguity about whether the horns or messengers 'must blast.' This reflects Greek relative clause structure rather than clear Hebrew syntax.
